texts: Pair-produces antimatter from gamma photons and holds it in a magnetic bottle.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 2$() machine.

Physics, briefly: a gamma photon with enough energy can become a particle and its antiparticle at once - $(thing)pair production$(), E = mc² run backwards. Antimatter annihilates on touching anything, so a $(thing)Penning trap$() holds it in vacuum with electric and magnetic fields alone. I check the seals twice a day.
Inverts the local arrow of time to harvest chronons.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 2$() machine.

Note to self: a $(thing)chronon$() is a hypothetical quantum of time, proposed in the 1920s and never adopted by physics. The arrow of time, though, is real: entropy rises, and that is why the past differs from the future. This machine flips it locally and catches what falls out.
Gravitationally focuses the invisible halo surrounding every galaxy.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 3$() machine.

Galaxies spin too fast for the matter we can see to hold them together. Something unseen supplies the missing gravity: $(thing)dark matter$(), about five times as much as ordinary matter, spread in a halo far beyond the visible disc. This collector gathers it - and the Nebular Gas my first stars are made from.
Separates a spray of particles by mass and charge: quark flavours, leptons and gauge bosons, one by one.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 2$() machine.

Real spectrometers work on the same idea: a magnetic field bends a charged particle's path, and how sharply it curves gives away its momentum and charge. Light particles swing wide, heavy ones barely turn. Mine sorts the spray into labelled bins.
A ring accelerator that smashes heavy nuclei into quark-gluon plasma.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 2$() machine.

Quarks are never seen alone - the strong force pulls harder the further apart they get. But smash heavy nuclei together hard enough and, for an instant, protons and neutrons melt into a soup of free quarks and gluons: the universe as it was a microsecond after the Big Bang.

Day 96. The $(item)Particle Spectrometer$() splits quark-gluon plasma into $(item)quark flavours$(), $(item)leptons$() and $(item)gauge bosons$(). The heaviest quarks and the $(item)Higgs$() need the Synchrotron.

The $(thing)Standard Model$() is our best account of matter: six quarks, six leptons, the gauge bosons that carry the forces, and the Higgs, whose field gives particles their mass. It is astonishingly accurate, and plainly incomplete - it has no gravity and no dark matter.

All of them together make the $(item)Standard Model Matrix$(). The Collider turns it and dark matter into $(item)Superpartner Shards$(), and the Tesseract Assembler unifies everything into a $(item)Grand Unified Core$().$(br2)Correction to my earlier notes: the Higgs Catalyst now needs a real Higgs boson.

A ring accelerator built from real beamline parts: bending dipoles, focusing quadrupoles, RF cavities, cryogenics, vacuum pumps and a detector hall. It makes the exotic hadrons nothing else can.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 3$() machine.

Like the collider, but a real beamline, and every part matters:$(li)dipoles bend$(li)quadrupoles focus$(li)RF cavities accelerate$(li)cryo jackets keep the magnets superconducting$(li)pumps keep the pipe empty$(li)the detector hall sees what was made

Why a ring: a magnetic field curves a charged beam, so the same cavities can kick it again on every lap. A synchrotron raises its field in step with the beam's energy - hence the name.$(br2)Better $(item)coils$() unlock heavier particles: $(item)Glueball Cores$() need tier 2, $(item)Hyperon Crystals$() tier 3.
Resonates a crystal lattice until it emits particles that travel faster than light.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 2$() machine.

A $(thing)tachyon$() is a hypothetical particle that always moves faster than light; in the equations its mass comes out imaginary. No experiment has ever found one. This crystal, apparently, has not read the literature. I have checked the readings four times.
